## Proof

We determine all polynomials $P(x) \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that $P(2017n)$ is prime for every natural number $n$.

**Constant polynomials work.** If $P(x) = p$ where $p$ is a fixed prime, then $P(2017n) = p$ is prime for every $n$. So every constant prime polynomial is a solution.

**No non-constant polynomial works.** Suppose for contradiction that $P$ is non-constant and $P(2017n)$ is prime for every natural number $n$. Define
$$Q(n) = P(2017n).$$
Since $P$ has integer coefficients and $2017 \in \mathbb{Z}$, the polynomial $Q \in \mathbb{Z}[n]$ is non-constant.

Pick any natural number $m$ and set $p = Q(m)$, which is prime by hypothesis. For every integer $k \geq 0$, the number $m + kp$ is a natural number, so $Q(m+kp)$ is prime.

**Key step.** For any polynomial $Q$ with integer coefficients, if $a \equiv b \pmod{p}$, then $Q(a) \equiv Q(b) \pmod{p}$. (Indeed, $Q(a)-Q(b) = \sum_i c_i(a^i - b^i)$, and each $a^i - b^i$ is divisible by $a - b$, hence by $p$.)

Since $m + kp \equiv m \pmod{p}$, we get
$$Q(m + kp) \equiv Q(m) = p \equiv 0 \pmod{p}.$$
Thus $p \mid Q(m+kp)$ for every $k \geq 0$. But $Q(m+kp)$ is prime, so the only possibility is
$$Q(m + kp) = p \quad \text{for all } k \geq 0.$$

This means the non-constant polynomial $Q(x) - p$ has infinitely many roots ($x = m, m+p, m+2p, \ldots$), which is impossible. Contradiction.

**Conclusion.** The only polynomials $P(x) \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ satisfying the condition are the constant polynomials $P(x) = p$, where $p$ is a prime number.

### PROOF COMPLETE
